report.summary: The only failure, test_deleted_book_disappears[chromium], is caused by a random stale-read cache in the app: list_books() in app/main.py serves a cached book list 70% of the time, and deletes never invalidate that cache, so the deleted row can still render after the redirect. The outcome is chance-dependent, so this is classified as flaky with the root cause in the app. First step: remove or invalidate the cache on writes (or drop the random branch) in app/main.py, then rerun the test several times to confirm it is stable.

causes.title: list_books() randomly returns a stale cached list after a delete
causes.explanation: app/main.py:148-157 keeps a per-user cache (_recent_lists). list_books() returns the cached list whenever the user is cached and random.random() < 0.7, and only rebuilds from the DB otherwise. books_delete() (app/main.py:343-350) and the API delete never clear or update _recent_lists. The test creates a book via the API, opens /books (which caches the list including the book), clicks delete, and is redirected to /books. That redirect render calls list_books() again, and with 70% probability it returns the stale list that still contains 'Delete me-6876d9f8'. The row therefore stays in the page and the count assertion sees 1 element. Because the page is rendered once and then only re-queried, all 14 polls see the same stale DOM, which matches the log. The same code passes roughly 30% of the time, so this is a timing/chance dependency, not a deterministic wrong behavior. The underlying defect is in the app (no cache invalidation on writes, plus the random branch), so the fix belongs in app/main.py, not in the test. Other tests that list books for the same user could also hit this intermittently.
evidence: Actual value: 1 / 14 × locator resolved to 1 element / unexpected value "1"
app/main.py:152: if user_id in _recent_lists and random.random() < 0.7:
app/main.py:343-350: books_delete() performs DELETE and redirects without touching _recent_lists
app/main.py:260: render_books() calls list_books(user["id"]) on every /books render
causes.suggested_fix: In app/main.py, remove the random.random() short-circuit from list_books() so it always reads from the DB (or delete _recent_lists entries on every book insert, update and delete, including in books_delete and api_delete_book). Simplest correct fix: always query the DB and drop _recent_lists. Then rerun tests/ui/test_books_ui.py repeatedly (e.g. 20 times) to confirm the failure no longer appears. Do not change the test; its assertion is correct for a delete that works.
